quests.instruction: Which word means the moment a vehicle leaves to start its journey?
quests.hint: Think about the exact moment your flight finally leaves the ground and begins its trip.
quests.explanation: Departure means the moment a vehicle leaves to start a trip. Every flight has a scheduled departure time!
quests.funFact: Airports often show a big board listing every flight's departure time!

quests.instruction: Which word means the moment a vehicle reaches its destination?
quests.hint: Think about the exact moment your flight finally touches down at your destination.
quests.explanation: Arrival means the moment a vehicle reaches its destination. Families often wait excitedly for an arrival!
quests.funFact: An arrival board at the airport shows exactly when each flight is expected to land!

quests.instruction: Which word means stepping onto a plane, train, or ship to begin a trip?
quests.hint: Think about walking down the jet bridge and stepping onto the airplane before it takes off.
quests.explanation: Boarding means stepping onto a vehicle to begin a trip. Passengers line up for boarding before departure!
quests.funFact: Airlines often let families with young children begin boarding a little earlier than everyone else!

quests.instruction: Which word means a short stop at another airport partway through a longer trip?
quests.hint: Think about a short wait at a middle airport before catching your very next connecting flight.
quests.explanation: A layover is a short stop partway through a trip. Travelers often wait at an airport during a layover!
quests.funFact: Some layovers are short, but others can last many hours between two connecting flights!

quests.instruction: Which word describes a trip from one place to another, especially a long one?
quests.hint: Think about the whole adventure of traveling from your home all the way to a faraway place.
quests.explanation: A journey is a trip from one place to another. A journey can be short or take many days!
quests.funFact: Every long journey is really made up of many small, exciting steps along the way!

quests.instruction: Which word describes a long trip, especially one taken by ship or into space?
quests.hint: Think about a long, exciting trip across the wide ocean or even out into space.
quests.explanation: A voyage is a long trip, especially by ship or into space. Sailors and astronauts both go on a voyage!
quests.funFact: Famous explorers once set sail on long voyages to discover new lands across the ocean!

quests.instruction: Which word means the regular trip someone takes between home and work or school?
quests.hint: Think about the same trip you take to school or work, again and again, every single day.
quests.explanation: A commute is the regular trip between home and work or school. Many people commute by car, bus, or train!
quests.funFact: A shorter commute gives someone a little more free time at the start and end of every day!

quests.instruction: Which word describes many cars stuck moving very slowly or not at all on a busy road?
quests.hint: Think about a long line of cars barely moving at all during a very busy time on the road.
quests.explanation: A traffic jam is many cars stuck moving slowly. Traffic jams often happen during a busy rush hour!
quests.funFact: Traffic reports on the radio help drivers know which roads to avoid during a big traffic jam!

quests.instruction: Which word describes the busiest time of day when the most people are traveling to or from work?
quests.hint: Think about the busy time each morning and evening when every road seems full of cars at once.
quests.explanation: Rush hour is the busiest travel time of day. Roads and trains are extra crowded during rush hour!
quests.funFact: Rush hour usually happens twice a day, once in the morning and once in the evening!

quests.instruction: Which word means taking a different, longer path because the usual road is blocked?
quests.hint: Think about following a different road because your usual street is closed for repairs.
quests.explanation: A detour is a different path taken when a road is blocked. Signs guide drivers along a detour!
quests.funFact: Following detour signs carefully helps drivers find their way even when their usual road is closed!

quests.instruction: Which word describes the path a vehicle follows to get from one place to another?
quests.hint: Think about the exact path your bus follows every day, turn by turn, to reach school.
quests.explanation: A route is the path a vehicle follows to reach a destination. A bus follows the same route every day!
quests.funFact: Planning a good route ahead of time can help make any trip much smoother!

quests.instruction: Which word describes the final place a traveler is heading toward?
quests.hint: Think about the exact place you are finally heading to at the very end of your trip.
quests.explanation: A destination is the final place a traveler is heading. Every trip has its own special destination!
quests.funFact: Choosing an exciting destination is often the very first step in planning a trip!

quests.instruction: Which word describes a written plan showing every stop and time of a trip?
quests.hint: Think about a written list showing exactly where you will go and when, during your whole trip.
quests.explanation: An itinerary is a written plan of a trip's stops. Travelers often carry an itinerary to stay organized!
quests.funFact: A clear itinerary helps a traveler know exactly what to expect at every part of their trip!

quests.instruction: Which word describes the paper or pass you need to be allowed to board a vehicle?
quests.hint: Think about the paper or pass you must show before you are allowed to board a train or plane.
quests.explanation: A ticket is a pass needed to board a vehicle. Passengers show their ticket before boarding!
quests.funFact: Many tickets today are stored right on a phone instead of printed on paper!

quests.instruction: Which word describes the special pass that shows your seat number for a flight?
quests.hint: Think about the pass with your name, seat, and gate number, shown right before you board a plane.
quests.explanation: A boarding pass is a special pass showing your flight details. Boarding passes show your seat and gate!
quests.funFact: A boarding pass often has a special code that gets scanned right before you step onto the plane!

quests.instruction: Which word describes the bags and suitcases a traveler brings on a trip?
quests.hint: Think about all the packed bags and suitcases you bring along on a big trip.
quests.explanation: Luggage is the bags a traveler brings on a trip. Luggage is often checked or carried onto a flight!
quests.funFact: Packing luggage carefully the night before a trip can help the morning feel much less rushed!

quests.instruction: Which word describes the goods carried by a ship, plane, or truck?
quests.hint: Think about all the boxes and goods being carried inside a big cargo ship or truck.
quests.explanation: Cargo is the goods carried by a vehicle. Ships, planes, and trucks all carry different kinds of cargo!
quests.funFact: Cargo can be almost anything, from fresh fruit to furniture to brand new cars!

quests.instruction: Which word describes goods transported in large amounts, especially by train or truck?
quests.hint: Think about the huge amounts of goods carried together on a very long train or truck.
quests.explanation: Freight is goods transported in large amounts. Freight often travels by train or truck!
quests.funFact: Moving freight by train can carry far more goods at once than a single truck ever could!

quests.instruction: Which word describes the money you pay to ride a bus, train, or taxi?
quests.hint: Think about the exact amount of money you pay before stepping onto a bus or into a taxi.
quests.explanation: A fare is the money paid to ride a vehicle. Passengers pay a fare before riding a bus, train, or taxi!
quests.funFact: Bus fares are sometimes cheaper for children, students, or older passengers!

quests.instruction: Which word describes the small fee drivers pay to use certain roads or bridges?
quests.hint: Think about the small fee a driver pays before crossing a special bridge or highway.
quests.explanation: A toll is a fee paid to use certain roads. Drivers pay a toll before crossing some highways and bridges!
quests.funFact: Money collected from tolls often helps pay to keep roads and bridges well maintained!

quests.instruction: Which word describes the fastest speed a driver is legally allowed to travel?
quests.hint: Think about the highest number of miles per hour a driver is allowed to go on a certain road.
quests.explanation: A speed limit is the fastest legal speed on a road. Speed limit signs help keep every driver safe!
quests.funFact: Speed limits change depending on the road, often slower near schools and faster on highways!

quests.instruction: Which word describes the gasoline or energy source that powers a vehicle's engine?
quests.hint: Think about the liquid a car needs in its tank before its engine can run at all.
quests.explanation: Fuel is the energy source that powers an engine. Vehicles need fuel to keep their engine running!
quests.funFact: Different vehicles use different kinds of fuel, like gasoline, diesel, or electricity!

quests.instruction: Which word describes the specific liquid fuel most cars burn inside their engine?
quests.hint: Think about the specific liquid pumped into most cars at a gas station to power their engine.
quests.explanation: Gasoline is a liquid fuel that most cars burn. Cars are filled with gasoline at a gas station!
quests.funFact: Gasoline is made from oil that comes from deep underground!

quests.instruction: Which word describes the part that stores electric power for an electric or hybrid vehicle?
quests.hint: Think about the part inside an electric car that stores power, just like the battery in a toy.
quests.explanation: A battery is a part that stores electric power. Electric and hybrid vehicles are powered by a battery!
quests.funFact: A large vehicle battery can be recharged by simply plugging it into a charging station!

quests.instruction: Which word describes the process of finding the way from one place to another?
quests.hint: Think about the whole process of figuring out exactly which roads to take to reach a new place.
quests.explanation: Navigation is the process of finding the way somewhere. Maps and GPS both help with navigation!
quests.funFact: People have used stars, maps, and now satellites to help with navigation throughout history!

quests.instruction: Which word describes the satellite system that helps a device show your exact location?
quests.hint: Think about the system your phone or car uses to show a little blue dot marking exactly where you are.
quests.explanation: GPS is a satellite system that shows your exact location. Cars and phones use GPS to help with directions!
quests.funFact: GPS uses signals from satellites orbiting far above the Earth to figure out your exact spot!

quests.instruction: Which word describes the tool with a needle that always points toward north?
quests.hint: Think about the small round tool with a spinning needle that always settles pointing north.
quests.explanation: A compass is a tool with a needle pointing north. Compasses help travelers know which direction to go!
quests.funFact: A compass needle always points north because it lines up with the Earth's own magnetic field!

quests.instruction: Which word describes a drawing that shows roads, places, and how to get from one spot to another?
quests.hint: Think about the paper or screen showing roads and towns, helping you plan exactly how to get somewhere.
quests.explanation: A map is a drawing showing roads and places. Maps help travelers plan the best way to get somewhere!
quests.funFact: The very first maps were drawn thousands of years ago to help people find their way!

quests.instruction: Which word describes a light or sound that gives drivers instructions, like stop or go?
quests.hint: Think about the light or sound that tells a driver exactly what to do next on the road.
quests.explanation: A signal is a light or sound giving instructions. Traffic lights and turn signals both give a signal!
quests.funFact: Clear signals help every driver on a busy road understand exactly what to do next!

quests.instruction: Which word describes the official card proving a person has passed a test to drive?
quests.hint: Think about the small card in a wallet proving that someone has passed their driving test.
quests.explanation: A license is an official card proving someone can drive. Drivers must earn a license before driving alone!
quests.funFact: Earning a license usually means passing both a written test and a real driving test!
